response.overview: Set along the stunning coast of Gunung Kidul, UNESCO Global Geopark, Yogyakarta, Java, Indonesia, Plastic Tourism explores the paradox of a tropical paradise threatened by plastic waste and uncontrolled tourism. Through immersive visuals and local voices, the film reveals the environmental impact while highlighting grassroots initiatives, from beach clean-ups to creative plastic recycling. At its heart are Javanese traditions and spirituality, including the Larungan ocean offering ceremony, an expression of gratitude and harmony with nature. The film concludes with a shadow puppet performance in which the Pandawa’s victory over the Kurawa symbolizes the triumph of selfless action (dharma) over ego, offering a reflection on environmental responsibility.
response.tagline: Plastic tourism shows the environmental  and ecological crisis caused by plastic waste generated from travel, resort stays, and high visitor volumes in a still preserve UNESCO Geopark in Indonesia
response.title: Plastic Tourism
